precepts.text: And after this I beheld, and lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea. So the winds are the armies of the earth. The winds are the armies of the earth, sent to subdue the man, also sent to bring destruction on this earth.
precepts.point: What is the wind that is going to blow on the earth? This cannot be a normal wind. It is windy every day. It is windy every single day. This is a different type of wind that is mentioned here in Revelation.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

precepts.why:
Four angels stand on the four corners of the earth, “holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea”. So what is the wind that is going to blow on the earth? It cannot be a normal wind. It is windy every single day. This is a different type of wind.

Ezra shows it: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” So the winds are the armies of the earth, gathered to subdue the man that came out of the sea, and sent to bring destruction on this earth.

Then the angel with the seal of the living God cries to the four angels, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The armies are held back; no destruction of mass proportions is coming until the hundred and forty and four thousand are sealed, and that seal is the law.

So if you truly want the end to come, you are going to be out here teaching your people and raising up the nation of Israel. The Most High God is waiting on a specific number, 144,000 unified in keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ, and then deliverance will come. The Christian church never even talks about the 144,000, because it is not about the deliverance of our people. Unity is the sweet savor of salvation.

precepts.text: This my son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations: the ICBM missiles, all that technology, their satellites across the globe. And shall destroy them without labour by the law, which is like unto fire. God is saying his law is fire.
precepts.point: Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan: our comings is supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings is after Satan. That goes back to Genesis 4.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
The Lord shall consume that Wicked “with the spirit of his mouth”, and 2 Esdras 13 shows the Son doing it: “this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest.”

Those wicked inventions are the ICBM missiles and all that technology, their satellites spread across the globe. Christ will rebuke all of it and “shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame.”

Then: “he shall destroy them without labour by the law.” He will not need their weapons; the law does the destroying. God is saying his law is fire, the same fire that is in the mouth of those who teach it. That is the spirit of his mouth and “the brightness of his coming” that destroys the Wicked in 2 Thessalonians 2.

precepts.point: And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel: these are the leaders here; 144,000 is just the leading men. In order for them to be sealed, they got to know who they are, at least to some extent. So how you going to read that and be confused about the 12 tribes? You just read all of the tribes there. note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Four angels hold the four winds of the earth, and another angel cries to them, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The four winds are held back for a reason, and Ezra shows what gathers from those four winds.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” That multitude out of number is their military, gathered from the four winds to fight against Christ, the man that came out of the sea.

So the holding of the winds is this: do not let war pop off to the max until the servants of God are sealed. The armies of the nations are held back until the leaders of Israel, the hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes, are sealed with the law of God in Christ.

precepts.text: Of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do. They were able to read the stars and lead the ships; they knew how to navigate the waters.
precepts.point: Semitic primarily refers to a major language family of the Middle East and the Horn of Africa which includes Hebrew, Arabic, and Aramaic: the people of Shem. But when it comes to the Israelites, the Most High is only dealing with the twelve tribes.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.” The tribes that left the heathen went into the Euphrates “by the narrow places of the river” and down into the ocean, and the Most High was with them. He showed them signs, and there were men among them able to read those signs.

“And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.” Issachar could read the stars. That is how they were the navigators: they had understanding of the times, they knew what Israel ought to do, and so they were able to lead the ships as the tribes came over. They knew how to navigate the waters.

They understood the winds and the currents, the Atlantic drift routes from Africa to America. Solomon understood all of this too, with the navy he had going out; the same ports Solomon’s navy knew were the stops along the route, because “through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. African boatmen from Lake Chad later built a papyrus boat on the pattern of the ancient Egyptians and sailed it from North Africa as far as Barbados, proving such a drift journey on the Africa-to-America currents could be done, because the currents were understood.

So the ten tribes did not wander blindly into “a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The Most High showed signs, Issachar read them, and the ships came across into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America. “Then dwelt they there until the latter time”, and that is why we are here in the latter times.

precepts.text: This is the counsel, and it is Cyrus speaking: who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel. And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts. That was the proclamation charged to Israel.
precepts.point: For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth. A year and a half of travel means stops along the way: the maritime ports. From the book Maritime Trade and the Movement of Culture, by the sister the teacher interviewed on the Quest voyage and whose museum in Charleston the nation plans to visit: the Red Sea and Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, trading gold, ivory, spices, and textiles with Arabia, India, Persia, and China, with cultural diffusion along the coasts.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration; 400 Years of Sweat Equity!

precepts.why:
Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

precepts.text: And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion-geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea. Hiram sent shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: the maritime men. And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents. Ezion-geber sits at the northern tip of the Red Sea's Gulf of Aqaba, near the region where the tribes entered the Euphrates. We had maritime trade going in Solomon's time, so it was no mystery for us to make it from Persia over to the Americas: the ports were there. Ivan Van Sertima's They Came Before Columbus speaks of Solomon's ships.

precepts.why:
“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

precepts.why:
Solomon’s ships “came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold”. Isaiah uses that same gold: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

We often read this and keep going, and some will say it is the best gold, but we don’t go deeper into what the gold of Ophir is. The gold of Ophir is an exceptionally fine, pure gold, prized in the ancient world, famous as what King Solomon and King Hiram of Tyre brought in, and its exact location remains one of history’s greatest archaeological mysteries.

That is what the Most High is going to make you men: that pure fine gold. The same tribes who crossed the waters on those old maritime routes, whose record the historians call mythical, are the men the Most High will make more precious than the golden wedge of Ophir.

precepts.text: The ten tribes carried away captive by the king of Assyria took counsel to leave the multitude of the heathen and go forth into a further country where never mankind dwelt, that they might there keep their statutes which they never kept in their own land. The journey was a year and a half, and the same region is called Arsareth.
precepts.point: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, but Joseph ruled all Egypt. Canaan wasn't ours yet, and Joseph already had the crown.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Ezra explains how Ephraim and Manasseh pushed the people “to the ends of the earth”: “Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.”

“But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,” “That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” “And they entered into Euphrates by the narrow places of the river.” “For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.”

“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth.” It took a year and a half to travel, and that region called Arsareth is the land now called America. That is how Joseph became the fruitful bough by a well in the western hemisphere, whose branches run over the wall.

There was gathered together a multitude of men out of number from the four winds of heaven to subdue him: they will have one consent, because the Most High is going to harden them like he did Pharaoh, and the popular persuasion is already laying the groundwork: let's all come together and fight the demons coming from space. He neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword nor any instrument of war; but he sent out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire, and it burnt them up every one, so that nothing was perceived but dust and smell of smoke.
precepts.point: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. There it is: gathered together, minds already persuaded. And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, and these both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Revelation says the armies were gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse and against his army. Ezra saw that same war. “there arose a wind from the sea”, and “that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled.” The man that came out of the sea is Christ, with the thousands of heaven, the armies that follow him.

And “whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” He speaks the laws out of his mouth, and the people just disintegrate, because they are guilty of that law. That is the sharp sword out of his mouth in Revelation, the laws of God.

Then “there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. They will have one consent, because the Most High is going to harden them like he did Pharaoh. And the popular persuasion is already laying the groundwork: let's all come together and fight the demons coming from space.

After this, “all they which were gathered together to subdue him were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.” Scared to death, but the Most High moves them. As Romans 9 shows, he built them up, just like ancient Egypt: Babylon the Great, this white man, this Edomite, built up just to be destroyed, made to fight against him.

And “he neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war”, but sent out of his mouth “a blast of fire”, “a flaming breath”, and “sparks and tempests”, and “burned them up every one, so that upon a sudden of an innumerable multitude nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.” Ashes to ashes, and dust to dust.

precepts.text: The historian Duran found confirmation in the promise that the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea: surely, he argued, this promise was fulfilled by the multitudes the Spanish found in the new world. He also noted the traditions of long journeys like the one from Assyria to Arzareth, traditions of flights like the Exodus from Egypt, manna falling from heaven, and an old man who began the tale of his people's origins with the words in the beginning, roughly parallel to Genesis. Why would so-called Indians be quoting the Bible unless they were Israelites?
precepts.point: Book read in class, Lost Tribes and Promised Lands by Ronald Sanders (1978): Columbus gave to the peaceable multitude of the islands the name Indios, because he considered their habitation to be the Indies, but perhaps also because he thought of them as living in God, en Dios. Columbus was reading the book of Esdras. The scriptures call them a peaceable multitude; the world called them noble savages.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

precepts.why:
“Afterward saw I the same man come down from the mountain, and call unto him another peaceable Multitude.” The same man is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah of Revelation 1, with feet like burnt brass and hair like wool. And the angel explains it: “he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him”, those are the ten tribes, the northern kingdom. That is who Christ gathers in these last days, through the work the prophets are doing in the worldwide blitzes, in Puerto Rico, Ecuador, Mexico, Chile.

The historians knew who that peaceable multitude was. Columbus gave the peaceable multitude of the islands the name Indios, because he took their home to be the Indies, but perhaps also because he thought of them as living in God, en Dios. Columbus was reading the book of Esdras. The scriptures call them a peaceable multitude; the world called them noble savages.

The historian Duran found more confirmation in Hosea: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.” Surely, he argued, that promise was fulfilled by the multitudes the Spanish found in the new world. Remember Israel blessed Ephraim and Manasseh to be a multitude of nations; that is what the Spaniards found.

Duran also noted that the Indians of Mexico had traditions of long journeys like the one from Assyria to Arzareth, flights like the Exodus from Egypt, earthquakes that swallowed evil men, manna falling from heaven, and an old man who began the tale of his people’s origins with the words in the beginning, like Genesis. Why would so-called Indians be quoting the Bible unless they were Israelites? We had books, we carried the Bible with us, and they stole our records.

So the peaceable multitude Christ calls is the ten tribes scattered on this side of the world, and Hosea’s promise stands over them: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

precepts.text: The Most High stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia in 539 BC, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled. Who is there among you of all his people? His God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the Lord God of Israel. Cyrus gave us freedom to go back; the ten tribes instead took counsel to go into a further country.
precepts.point: Book read in class, Lost Tribes and Promised Lands, on the Marrano navigator Montezinos: he heard an exclamation of thanksgiving that blessed God for not making the speaker an idolater, a barbarian, a negro, or an Indian, and it dawned on him: those Indians, they are Hebrews. Later, strangers who came by canoe told him in their common ancestral tongue that they were themselves of the tribe of Reuben, and that the tribe of Joseph lived on an island nearby. Ephraim and Manasseh make up the tribe of Joseph: the islands. They asked him to send twelve bearded men to be their teachers, for though they spoke Hebrew they could not read or write it. The sorcerers of Francisco's tribe had perceived that they were a special people who should be left alone, that the God of these children of Israel is the true God, that everything inscribed on their tablets is true, and that at the end of days they will be lords of all the nations of the earth. Montezinos turned the tale into propaganda for the Dutch conquest of Brazil; Esau turned even this knowledge into conquest.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

precepts.why:
“Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”. That was the Assyrian captivity, 722 BC; the northern kingdom was forcefully displaced into Assyria. Then Esdras says, “But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen”. That is a jump in history, into the Persian captivity, when Cyrus the Persian gave us freedom.

For our people who don't know that history, Ezra 1 shows it: “Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”. The Most High moved the king of Persia in 539 BC. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.”

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem”. His people: not Persians, but Israelites, God's people. “And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Whether we were in Assyria or in Persia, wherever we were scattered and displaced, we were given freedom to go back to Israel and build the house of God.

That is what 2 Esdras 13 is recording. The ten tribes were given that freedom, but they took counsel to go instead “into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” The northern kingdom wanted a fresh start, tired of captivity after captivity: Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian. So they went into Arsareth, the land Columbus identified as America. Our land is Israel; we were not always in the islands.

note.label: America: The New Roman Empire

precepts.why:
The lion charges the eagle: “For the earth hast thou not judged with truth.” America set herself up as the police of the earth, but she has not judged the earth with truth. “For thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable.” The meek is Judah, and the peaceable is the northern kingdom, and Ezra proves it.

“Afterward saw I the same man come down from the mountain, and call unto him another peaceable Multitude.” The man from the mountain is Christ, and when he comes he calls unto him another peaceable multitude. That peaceable multitude is Israel, the tribes he gathers. So when the lion tells the eagle “thou hast hurt the peaceable”, he is speaking of the same people he calls to himself.

“Thou hast loved liars”: if you lie you can be their friend, a senator, a mayor. They sat in Congress and lied, especially about the Epstein files, all of them lying. And they “destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit, and hast cast down the walls of such as did thee no harm.” The northern kingdom here did them no harm, and they said destroy them, and enslaved them.

That is why “thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest.” What America did to the peaceable and the meek of the earth has come up before the Most High, and he has considered it.

The angel explains the vision to Ezra: “And whereas thou sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him”, those are the ten tribes. So when the lion says to the eagle, “thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable”, it is the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom. The eagle afflicted both.

The northern kingdom here did them no harm, and they cast down their walls, destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit, and enslaved them. That wrongful dealing and that pride has come up unto the Highest.

“The Highest also hath looked upon the proud times, and, behold, they are ended, and his abominations are fulfilled.” The proud times are the time of their technology. “And therefore appear no more, thou eagle, nor thy horrible wings, nor thy wicked feathers nor thy malicious heads, nor thy hurtful claws”, the militaries, “nor all thy vain body”, the citizens. This is the end of the eagle.
